reviews.text: Давно слежу за интерпретацией славянской мифологии от Папсуева. Очень вахоподобный визуал. Мне очень нравится. Так что по визуалу однозначно 5. Музыка супер. Крайне удачно дополняет игровой процесс и визуал игры. Так что 5. Что касается игрового процесса. Не забываем, что это рогалик. Довольно увлекательные бои. Казалось бы, карточками раскидываешься, а не замечаешь, как сидишь и считаешь, что и как прокинуть и так далее. Время пролетает незаметно. Поскольку в данной категории игр не очень-то и много, то могу точно сказать, по моему мнению, что это будет один из ярких представителей декбилдеров. Так что несмотря на баги и всякие огрехи, свойственные для ранних доступов, ставлю 5. Ну и не могу не отметить, что это игра наша, отечественная. За это также однозначно ставлю 5. Всячески надо поддерживать наших ребят там, где есть такая жуткая конкуренция за внимание игроков.

The game looks very nice and I particularly like the design of the monsters. I know it's a work in progress, but I wish the rest was already just as great as the overall graphics. While the game is playable in it's current stage of development, I think it still needs quite a bit of work to actually challenge some of the other deck builders out there. There are some mechanics and even monsters that resemble quite a bit of those seen in Slay the Spire, which is alright. And there are original ideas as well, like the fact that all the dead enemies stay on the battlefield for a couple of rounds, creating obstacles and opportunities. This was an interesting feature. However, the actual deck building in Deathless soon starts to feel like a sluggish chore. Even after unlocking all the currently available cards I felt that they didn't offer much variety. Furthermore, while the individual fights take quite a while to complete (you might spend up to 20 minutes chipping away a boss monster's health bar), during a playthrough there aren't enough opportunities to add cards to your deck, remove them or upgrade them to come up with zany decks and fun combos. The lack of variation doesn't make the fights hard - it just makes them less interesting. I definitely see potential, but I'm hoping for more complex card unlocks and more content overall before I can recommend this one. Personally, I don't mind playing an ugly looking game if it has a good flow. Deathless is the opposite, it looks great but on the long run it's tedious to play. That's why I'm giving this one thumbs down for now. I might change my mind later, depending on the updates.

I think the game is well made and the art looks great. I would recommend waiting for a sale. The reason I don't recommend it is because I feel most of my runs have been pretty anaemic and unsatisfying: it's quite rare to get a synergistic build going before you bleed out and while there's some archetypes to aim for they don't mix well which means you can get stuck with a deck that's less than the sum of its parts. Difficulty progression being tied to each character is a bit of a slog, new unlocks/upgrades being paired with new negative modifiers makes the power progression seem like a net-neutral or even net-negative (unlocking curses felt like a huge setback). I was never a big fan of relics that give you bonuses for keeping bad cards (basics, curses, statuses etc) unless they were particularly strong which they aren't in this game. Honestly it's probably one of the better offerings in the genre but also one of the more expensive and not worth the price in its current state imo.

I don't know why this game doesn't get more visibility within the Rogue-like Deckbuilder niche... It clearly draws inspiration from and heavily clones Slay the Spire, but unlike 90% of the other clones, this game does it brilliantly. You get 4 different characters right from the start, each with unique decks and strategies to follow, as well as their own bosses and unique events along the way. The balancing makes for a solid challenge without becoming frustrating or overwhelming. The cards you unlock through each run feel genuinely rewarding for future playthroughs. Animations are far more polished than the average for the genre. The narrative also has more depth than in many other games in this niche. It's a very enjoyable experience if you're looking for a deckbuilder inspired by Slay the Spire that will keep you hooked, offer a challenge, and not make you drop it after 3 runs for being a mediocre failed clone like so many others. If I had to point out one minor flaw, it would be the repetitive soundtrack.

是类塔游戏里很出色的一个作品，音乐和美术都很不错，通过控制对手站位来规避和制造伤害是本作的核心机制，初上手卡组成型难度较大，熟练之后难度适中。由于大部分卡的设计没有翻倍的机制，所以数值膨胀不快，爽感相对低一些（当然也有几个流派数值涨的挺快），更多是一种运营过程的乐趣（没错，就是用一手烂牌磨死不死之神)。 个人认为四个角色里由易到难排序分别是：瓦尔瓦拉，多布里尼亚，瓦茜莉萨，阿廖沙。建议先用前面两个打过不死之神后再尝试后面两个，不然可能会有点折磨。 然后英雄之路中间那个大门啥时候开启，期待一手。

This game did leave me scratching my head. It didn't leave a bad taste in my mouth - the point is I kind of was expecting more from it and it left an impression of "overpromising and underdelivering". Strengths: + Lore and idea is simply superb, the atmosphere is truly magical - 10/10 + art - game devs, give your designers a proper raise, they do deserve it, the artwork is simply stunning - 10/10 Meeeh: - The story. Gosh, this game and its story had all the potential of becoming the next 'Black Book' and had an engaging and intriguing beginning, but at the end it felt kind of ... incomplete? I was hoping for it to be longer because of the storyline, not because of the endless fights. - Some cards and some characters' abilities are straightup confusing and questionable. - It's really hard to build a good deck, so at one point the game turns into a hunt for decent cards. - The enemies, on the other hand, are sometimes too hard to beat even if your difficulty level is 'for puss... chicken' (I always choose that). Sooo, it's not THAT bad - it might be worth checking out when it is on sale. For me it's a 5/10, it leaves much to be desired and I won't play it again.

Animations are nice at first - but become annoying af later on, you wish you could skip it entirely. Initially a solid 7/10 - after some time spent it drops off hard to a 4/10

Moving the enemies around tactically to defend or attack is a wonderful mechanic but of all characters, only the default one really uses this mechanic and there is the most fun to play. Sadly because if the other characters would be as good, the game would be amazing. Still its a pretty fun and creative game and i recommend it. Especially on sale.

[i]Very Solid Card Battler[/i] Deathless; Hero Quest is a welcome addition to the higher echelon of card battlers. The game delivers the basics of the genre well and does a good job of weaving the roguelike elements into the game while still allowing the player to make some tough route decisions. Strong play style variety exists between the 4 selectable characters. Furthermore, the variety continues to the bosses which are distinctly different in terms of tactics they try to use against the player; especially true for the “legendary” bosses and final. Difficulty really ramps up on these bosses and the final boss definitely pushes your deck to the limit which can be a bit jarring the first few times around. Player agency remains high with good ability to control what cards get added/removed/upgraded in your deck. However, above avg. rate cards in each character’s card pools are fairly limited; leading to some narrow selection choices. Visually, there is a nice variety of enemies you’ll encounter on a run. A few of the animations are a little stiff and lacking in my opinion, they are still ok but I think they could have been better. Overall, this one is definitely worth checking out.

I wasn't sure what I was going to get with this game, and I was pleasantly surprised. It's solid. If you like Slay the Spire, this has a lot in common with it. It also has some interesting new mechanics, which can be confusing until you learn them. For example, monsters that you "defeat" stay on the battlefield and block you from attacking living enemies and block melee attacks from enemies. Enemy positioning is a critical strategy in this game too. Pros: * Solid gameplay with interesting mechanics * You can see the rewards you get from each encounter and choose accordingly * Encounters have modifiers which makes the "direction" choice more interesting * You can postpone regular boss fights until it is convenient, but they will get stronger if you wait * Interesting and unique lore * The art and attack animations are nice bonuses * Each character plays differently, leading to a lot of replay value Areas for Improvement: * There are a lot of new mechanics that require a few playthroughs to understand * It would be very nice if the right mouse click would cancel a card drag instead of doing nothing * You must play the game at full resolution in order to have readable tooltips and numbers. Even then, it can be hard to read. The text is TINY! On that note, I'd actually prefer to have large icons for the encounter rewards, and maybe a book icon with a tooltip giving you the "story" explanation of the rewards. Right now most of the display area is taken up by text describing the fight and rewards in an in-character manner, when all I do is hover over the tiny icons at the bottom to see what the actual rewards / buffs / debuffs are. * The end-game is very difficult. For example, you can breeze through the first 3 bosses, and then, depending on your meta-progress, you might be expected to fight 4 legendary bosses in a row, followed by the ultimate boss? The characters have unique strengths geared against ONE legendary boss, so it's not realistic to expect up to 4 legendary bosses to be beatable with the same character. While it's a cool idea story-wise to have all the legendary bosses as optional-yet-kind-of-required bosses at the end, it would be less frustrating simply to have them unlock and grant you their item if you've beaten them with any character before (meta progression instead of per-game). In summary, if you want an StS-like game with a lot of replay value, this is a good one. Just be ready for a learning curve. Pick it up on sale!
